What [snorts] is one thing that you think that sales teams inside of these ISVs can do to enable themselves to win more enterprise software deals alongside those channel teams and their partners? >> Yeah, I I think um the most successful reps that we've seen at places like you know Twistlock and HashiCorp and GitHub and these organizations that became really big is that you don't view the channel team or the channel organization as like a completely separate service that may bring you some leads or may bring you some pipeline or whatever, that you take responsibility for your account list or your territory or your region or whatever it is, and you take ownership of engaging with people and partners that sell into your accounts rather than relying on the channel team to to do that for you. >> Mhm. >> I sell direct and the channel team does the channel bit and then, you know, they should be bringing me leads and they should be bringing me the most successful reps. View this as I have to sell into these 10 accounts. I'm going to go and engage with everybody who sells into these accounts. I'm going to find who's able to and willing to help me >> Yep. >> um and take ownership themselves, make the call themselves, engage with the partner themselves, because if you're relying on the channel team, you've probably got two channel resources covering all of North America. >> Yeah. >> Um they're good at assisting, they're good at supporting, they're good at, you know, the the enablement of the partner on a more programmatic level. >> Mhm. >> But if you want to do a deal in an account, you identify the partner that you want to who sells into that account, you go and find the right contact, you go and find what they're going to want in order to help you, >> Mhm. >> and you make that happen. And that really is the fastest way to to maximize your output is get more people selling for you. But relying on, you know, an external team to do that, really it's your responsibility. >> Yep. Uh the ownership should be on you to give more than you receive in the initial uh first quarter or second quarter, whether that is leads, data, information. A lot of times it might be deals uh that you could probably take direct or, you know, do uh by yourself, but uh using a partner to be able to do it, you're giving them an incentive on uh you know, running a deal, getting involved in uh running a sales cycle for your product. And I think stuff like that is oftentimes overlooked. You're going to have to give something to get something. In um this particular case, using channel partners, you got to give them some deals, some data, some leads in order to get more coming back to you. So uh yeah, it might seem like counter productive doing that day one, but ultimately it's going to get you more back in return. >> Definitely some misconceptions around this though. Like the very common objections we hear. Well, reseller is going to want 40%. >> Yep. >> True or not true? >> No, not true. Resellers are open to doing low margin transactions, especially for end users and accounts that they're already in place with and the ones that they already have a foothold in. So oftentimes it could be something like 5%, maximum 10% you know, as as a distributor and a value added reseller together. But yeah, the misconception often is that the reseller and the channel wants 30, 40, 50%. Not the case. >> Yeah. Other one is well then I won't be in control of the deal. Reseller is going to take control of the deal. Also true, false? >> Yeah, incorrect again. So [clears throat] control is often something that has a big question mark on it. If you loop in a value added reseller or a partner, is control going to be lost? Not the case. Control ultimately still sits with the ISV and the ISV rep. However, it's you know, orchestration at this point you're playing quarterback. You're able to throw the ball over to the reseller whenever the quote needs to be sent out and you can dictate exactly what the terms are, what the product exactly is, the SKU, all of that's dictated by you. The control ultimately still lies with you as the ISV rep. You just have an extension to your team in the partner sharing quotes and sharing terms with the end user. And it's more like you having another person going into battle for you, with you. Not necessarily somebody who's coming into their control. >> Yeah. I think a lot of the teams that we that we work with is you know, we have on the new business side and pipe generation and working with partners, identifying the right partners for [snorts] entering into new accounts and opening up deals. But also we work a lot with renewal teams and it's a team strategy. Leveraging partners for what they're good in certain deals >> Mhm. >> allows you to focus on the things that you want to focus on. So typically for a renewal team at a at an ISB, we want them to be engaging directly with the key senior stakeholders of the account, most likely more technical. >> Mhm. >> Um what the partner can do is they can they can remove a lot of procurement administration, right? Chasing up of hey, did you get the quote? Is the pricing correct? Where is it in the system? When are we getting the PO? All of these things are work and admin that ultimately if you're if you're handling it all on your own >> Mhm. >> you have to do. >> Yep. >> Um [snorts] whether this is new business or renewal, push the lower value admin down to people who specialize in doing that kind of thing. This is why resellers will be happy to take 5% if they're just doing this part of the sales cycle. Allows your ISB teams, and this is for sales leaders, removing that admin for the cost of 5 or 10% of of a deal should give back 30% of your sales team's time. If you're from from a sales cycle perspective, I'd say our experience is that 30% of a sales cycle, technical win is done, procurement, >> Yep. >> contracts, chasing, updates, admin. You need them on top of what's going on, and that's where they need to communicate with the partner. But do they need to be sending those emails? Do they need to be making the quotes? Do they need to be chasing up the contracts? Partners doing that for the sake of 5 or 10% and your rep is spending 30% more time speaking to technical decision makers, prospecting into new accounts, they're going to do more than 10% additional revenue. So I think for us it's all about picking the right partner for the right role. The misconceptions around high margin or they're in charge of the deal, if I hand over the deal or it takes, you know, 9 months to get onboarded with a reseller, >> Mhm. >> they're always around all of those things and an optimal channel doesn't operate that way. Um so uh I think there's a lot of misconceptions there. The most successful companies in the world are indirect companies. >> So, where does Lewisi play its part in this journey with these ISV? >> Yeah, and what we uh what we do is we we build [sighs] we build software to streamline this process. So, the interaction point between ISVs and resellers, how can we ease that process that I just talked about? So, that could be how do you identify, engage and activate a partner? Um we offer a software platform on top of a large data graph that will allow you to identify the right partners for the right thing. Do you need a service delivery partner to help you work with a manufacturing company in Germany? Do you need someone who sells into Deutsche Bank? Two very different situations, two potentially very different partners that you require. We have the data. Millions of data points have been analyzed and built into uh coverage map of 10,000 largest companies in the world, many thousand partners and what they do, who they do it for and and who they sell to. >> Mhm. >> Um we're here to help ISVs identify the right kind of partners and then recommend the kind of [snorts] activities that are going to engage that partner. Are they more interested in services? Are they looking for license resale revenue? Do they want to build out a security practice? All of this information is information we've gathered through years of working with these partners, understanding what they do. When you layer AI over the top of that, you get a really powerful tool to extract this this information. So, for us, it's about bringing the right partners to the right people inside an ISV, number one. Number two is streamlining that actual transaction process. >> Mhm. >> So, a um framework of contractual agreements with hundreds of thousands hundreds and thousands of partners around the world, allowing an organization to quickly connect, engage, quote, transact through that partner network without needing to go through that onboarding process, maintaining compliance, maintaining visibility, maintaining control like we talked about. >> Yeah. Ultimately, Lewis I, we are a helping hand in assisting you as an ISV grow your business. So whether you are looking to expand your product into newer markets, you would like to locate and identify net new partners in different geographical locations, whether you would like to transact particular deals in different regions, Lewis is able to assist on all of that and beyond. So it all starts with asking the question, you know, getting in contact with Luke, myself, the rest of our team, and figuring out what the art of the possible is. So if there are anybody or if there are any ISVs out there that would like to probably find out more, get in touch and we'd love to speak to you. >> Amazing. For those ISVs that perhaps have this problem at scale or that haven't even started to build their go-to-market, things like that, what is your general advice on where to start to solve this type of challenge? >> Yeah, in our experience, there are three stages of of company that we work with, three three stages of ISV that we work with. There are those who are usually up to Series B, launching the product, trying to get revenue, trying to find product-market fit, grow as fast as possible. Those type of organizations need to be able to operate as quickly as they can. For them, right now, I would say that investing time in building a partner program, channel organization which is orientated around new business generation and complicated [snorts] architecture deployments, implementation services, this kind of stuff, probably a bit too early for that. What you need to know is how can I transact with my potential customers as fast and efficiently as possible so that you get those wins, get those logos, get that revenue to get you to the Series B C mark, which is when you've proven to the market, going back to that topic of you're trying to recruit these people on a commission only basis, they're probably not going to be interested until you've got 100 customers, until you're at 50 to 100 million in revenue. So for the first phase, just find the most efficient ways of transacting with these enterprise customers, which in our experience is a professional procurement-orientated bar, someone who already has existing contracts with these large enterprises who can ease the process and get it done much much faster. You're going from a nine month onboarding process to a three week sales cycle if you leverage an existing supplier into an enterprise. So that's where I would suggest that that those smaller companies get get started. >> Mhm. >> You get to that point of where you've got the revenue and the the channel and the the partners are interested in coming to you and engaging with you. That's when you need to start putting together a program for how you can sell together. >> Mhm. >> What are the things that those partners need to say to their customers to go and build practices around your product, what services can they deliver? That's when you hire a channel team. You know, you go from having someone who handles the channel to a team that are out there proactively [snorts] identifying, engaging and selling to to the right kind of partners with the right kind of motion. And then the final phase is you go an IPO. You're you're near a billion dollars in revenue. You're looking to build an essentially maintain an ecosystem. You've recruited the partners, they're out there, they built practices, they're landing new customers. How do you keep them happy? How do you keep them productive? How do you keep them enabled? How do you roll out new products to them? How do you get them doing more? And this is this is the final phase And this is where you should work typically with distribution companies or companies like us who can help that at scale offer software-based enablement and delivery. But fundamentally that's when you get to the stage of a Palo Alto or a Microsoft where you're maintaining your ecosystem. So those are the three phases. >> Mhm. >> I think we go back to the mistakes that we see being made is that people leave a company who is in one phase to go to a company that's in a different phase and try and use what they're doing or the playbooks or the model to go back and someone leaves a Palo Alto and goes to a Series A company and says, oh we need to recruit 100 partners and we need a distributor who can do widespread enablement. You don't need that at that phase. So I think for us that's how we see it. Three companies we help, we have tools in each space. They build on each other. That's where we tend to start. >> Yeah, and the mistake that a lot of ISVs that I've worked with historically have made is if they are going to market they would go out and recruit 50, 100, 200 partners, spend a lot of time getting them up to speed on the product, what the solution does and you know, this in theory it sounds like the right thing to do but oftentimes you're recruiting partners which are then just sat there waiting for you to share more leads and data with them and ultimately you cause a bigger problem for yourself where you have 200 recruited partners and 195 of them don't have anything to do and they're just sat there and you wasted all this time there. So it's better to work with a company like Lewis Silo where we can identify the right caliber partner for you. We can identify identify which markets they're probably going to excel at and where they're going to do the best work and then ultimately make it a slow phased process instead of going at you know all 200 500 partners at once. That would be my suggestion. >> What do you think the channel blueprint should be for smaller ISVs? >> [sighs and gasps] >> Yeah, for smaller ISVs, don't overcomplicate the channel program. Number one, don't make it too complicated. Number four, program on its own isn't going to isn't going to lead to anything. Um, you need to understand you are the small fish in the pond when you're a small ISV. You need to be given something to get something. Like here says, right? If you want to go and build a channel at all, what are you putting skin in the game wise to incentivize a partner to work with you? Channel blueprint for me, if I'm series A and you know, we've worked with many CROs, CEOs at series A companies is make sure that you are as easy as possible to do business with for your customers, which means make sure that you are listed to be purchased on every cloud marketplace. Make sure that you have contracts and partners and network of partners in place which allows your customer to buy from whom they want to buy from in as easy a fashion as possible. That is pretty much all you need from a channel at that point because [clears throat] you are just trying to get to that $100 million number which proves to the rest of the ecosystem that it's worth investing in your company and the companies want to buy it. So channel blueprint very simple at the beginning. Just be available in places that your customers want to buy it and be as easy to transact with as possible. >> In your experience, what changes are you seeing in the expectation from channel and partner teams inside the ISV? And how does that change over the last five, 10, 15 years? >> Yeah, um, depends very much on the person. Um, and again, if people are going from a stage three company down to a stage one company and then not aware of the differences that you need at the those those things they can be spending their time on the wrong thing. Generally [snorts] speaking, there are multiple avenues to market which didn't exist five years ago. Things like cloud marketplaces. We now see the Cloud has own marketplace. Channel teams are trying to navigate this world where people have enormous spending commitments with cloud providers. They want to purchase through routes like buying through their Amazon EDP. But the primary motion of generating business for their company has been led by channel partners. What if that channel partner is not able to partake in that transaction? [snorts] This this split between who runs the sales cycle and which route the customer wants to buy through, that's something which is fairly new. And we see a lot of channel organizations either addressing it well through things like CPPO or running them in complete silos, which in our opinion is not the right way to do it. So I feel like with channel teams and what they're doing and what they're seeing is that they're trying to capitalize on the trends the same as everyone else tapping into AI motions, AI projects, AI budgets, but then also marketplaces in general, predominantly the three cloud providers, but then also adjacent ISV marketplaces, Snowflake and Salesforce and these kind of organizations. And then trying to figure out a way to to to combine the two motions of, you know, the traditional way that they've done things or the reseller motion with these new modern routes to market. So I'd say those are the main things that we've seen we've seen change. >> Another expectation that the ISV and the channel sales within an ISV will have is that, you know, a partner has a black book of contacts and by you partnering up with the reseller or the the channel partner that you can open up all these different doors and often times it can be done, but to have high expectations that you're going to walk into now 50 new meetings and new potential clients, I think it's probably the wrong approach to have. The best thing would be to, you know, lay down a good formula for how the channel partner can actually introduce your product into the end user using, you know, whether it's a technical session, maybe some workshops, maybe you know, some solution orientated seminar that can be delivered to the end user. That's probably a better way of going about it as opposed to just 50 net new meetings set up in your diary. So wrong expectation to have, but with the right help, I think it can be achieved just at a slower pace. >> Yeah, I it's kind of broadened than just the channel team, but it's it's the same sort of mistake again, which is that if I hire a channel person, the channel's going to start bringing me pipeline. Organisations who go down that road because they cannot generate enough pipeline themselves through either marketing, direct outreach, or whatever, channel is not a last resort, but it is a well, we're only doing this because we need them to bring pipeline, but you're not able to do it yourself. >> Mhm. >> If you can't do it, why do you think the ecosystem is going to want to do it for you? I think that there's that's definitely a misconception that we've seen is that channel could be a shortcut, and it can help for sure. You can work with a couple of partners, you can go out there and do a really great job for you. >> Yep. >> The hard yards of zero to 100 million, you have to do it. Expecting insights, CDW, SHI, you know, the big VAR players that are out there to care about you at all, you have to be one in a thousand vendors in order to really be [snorts] something that they that they choose to adopt. And the reality is that until you pass the test and get to a size where you matter to them, >> Mhm. >> you have to do the majority of this yourself. Uh it goes back to that early stage plan. What would we suggest? Be as efficient as possible. It allows you to do more deals faster, focus more of your time on the high value stuff, which is direct touch selling, going and speaking to customers. Get the transaction done as quickly as possible through whichever route the customer wants to buy through >> Mhm. >> so that you have got to the point where now you can have a little bit of expectation. >> Yeah. >> You've proven it out in the market. You've got the customers who are going to stand by your solution. You've got the revenue that you can be sharing around with a few [music] other people. That's when you can have expectations as a as a channel team.

metadata.title: SaaS Partners & Resellers [Lessons From 30+ Client Projects]
metadata.author: Willingness to Pay
metadata.shortDescription:
Building a partner sales channel in SaaS is hard and requires an understanding of a few key fundamentals. You're going to learn in full my framework for partners, resellers, White label partners, and reverse partnerships, how to structure the partner commissions and what to focus on in the legal relationship.

A lot of times, the growth that you expect will come from having partners doesn't happen. Why is that and how can you avoid it?

0:00 Why partner and reseller channels often fail in SaaS
2:16 Four partner types by customer ownership and product brand
11:09 Partners as an alternative to your own sales funnel and CAC
15:06 What a partner is worth depending on where they join the funnel
17:54 The cost of finding, signing and supporting partners
20:04 Silent partners and an ACV that does not fit the partner
26:04 How much help partners need to actually sell
30:40 Partner commissions, front loading and cost plus payment
38:16 How front loading partner pay affects valuation and fundraising
44:15 Summary and why direct sales should work first

If you like the video and want to keep learning about SaaS pricing ➢ Subscribe to the channel here: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCPsiSZ0K6iETeXno8PJmgDg?sub_confirmation=1

About me: I Global Expert on B2B SaaS Pricing Models, Monetisation, and Acquisition Strategies. 3x previous founder (3 exits) and now an advisor, investor, and board member. I've done commercial redesigns for over 100+ other B2B SaaS businesses across Europe, Asia, and North America. For more visit here: https://www.willingnesstopay.com/03-about

I’ve helped companies such as Microsoft, AGFA, SAP, Intel, and Samsung - and portfolio companies of VCs such as Bessemer, Tiger Global, and Gradient.

The Pricing Roadmap - my upcoming book on B2B SaaS Pricing via Houndstone Press (est. late 2022)... Visit here and sign up to get notified when the pre-order opens: https://www.willingnesstopay.com/saas-pricing-book

I create this content because this is the next level for me. I already have a 7-figure solo consulting practice doing something I really love, but I can only serve a handful of clients a year. So this is for all the rest of you as I believe all good SaaS products deserve to be good SaaS businesses. 

Enjoy the videos and don't forget to follow my channel for more on SaaS Pricing.
➢ Website: https://www.willingnesstopay.com/ 
➢ Linkedin: https://www.linkedin.com/in/ulriklehrskovschmidt

Thank you for your support! I love to hear from you, so please continue to comment, like, and favorite. If there is a topic or issue you want me to cover? Go ahead and leave a comment and I'll have it up for you soon!

Contact with… 
➢ Mail: ulrik@willingnesstopay.com 
#SaaSFunding #fundingforbusiness #SaaS #SaasPricingStrategy

metadata.title: How to Set Up Reseller Partners | PartnerPortal Tutorial
metadata.author: PartnerPortal io
metadata.shortDescription:
Learn how to set up reseller partners in PartnerPortal: partners who resell your product instead of referring customers to you. This tutorial covers the big difference from referral partners, who collects the customer's money, and how to set up both kinds of reseller program in your partner relationship management (PRM) portal.

In this video:
• Referral vs reseller: who bills the customer, and why resellers keep a margin instead of earning a commission
• Setting your portal's compensation model to Reseller on the Partner Model card
• When the partner collects: nothing is owed, and the margin is estimated for your reporting
• Reseller lead matching: tagging each invoice with the lead's website domain, in Stripe, QuickBooks or Xero
• A catch-all lead for a reseller's own wholesale orders
• Letting resellers update a lead's phase, close date and close value
• Lead phases, HubSpot stage mapping and two-way sync
• What your reseller sees when they move a deal
• When you collect: margin rates in your partner tiers, and paying the reseller their margin
• Adding a payout and reading its receipt: revenue, margin rate, wholesale price and the margin you owe
• Setting a different model for a partner group, one partner, or one lead

Chapters:
0:00 Introduction: who collects the money
0:33 The Partner Model card
1:09 Reseller lead matching
1:40 A catch-all lead
1:59 Letting resellers update their deals
2:25 CRM stage mapping and two-way sync
2:40 What your reseller sees
2:52 When you collect: margin tiers
3:11 Adding a payout and its receipt
3:28 A different model for a group, partner or lead

Reseller partners documentation: https://www.partnerportal.io/docs/partners/reseller-partners
Payment settings: https://www.partnerportal.io/docs/portal-setup/payment-settings
Commission and margin tiers: https://www.partnerportal.io/docs/payments/how-to-set-up-and-manage-commission-tiers
Sync leads to your CRM: https://www.partnerportal.io/docs/leads/sync-leads-to-your-crm

PartnerPortal is partner relationship management (PRM) software for running referral and reseller partner programs: https://www.partnerportal.io

segments.text: Welcome to PartnerPortal. In this short video, we'll show you how to set up reseller partners: partners who resell your product, instead of referring customers to you.
The biggest difference is who collects the customer's money. With referral partners, you bill the customer, and pay the partner a commission.
With resellers, the reseller usually owns the customer relationship. They bill the customer and keep their margin, and you bill them the wholesale price. So there's no commission to pay.
You set this up in Payment Settings, on the Partner Model card. Ledgerwick pays referral commissions today.
Click the pencil, and set the compensation model to Reseller. Rate fields across your portal now show margin instead of commission.
Next, choose who collects payment from the customer. For most reseller programs, that's the partner.
When the partner collects, nothing is owed to them here. You may not know what they charged their customer. If you set a margin rate, the portal estimates their margin for your reporting.
Reseller lead matching ties your revenue to the right lead. Your invoice goes to the reseller, so it can't tell us which of their customers it's for.
So tag each invoice with the lead's website domain, and enter the tag's name here.
Where the tag goes depends on your accounting system: Stripe, QuickBooks, or Xero. Our docs show each one.
Save. Any payouts you've already made keep the terms they were made with.
Sometimes a reseller's revenue has no named customer, like their own wholesale orders. For that, create one catch-all lead.
Assign it to the reseller, mark it Won, and use the reseller's own website. Tag those invoices with that domain, and they land on this lead.
Resellers usually run the sale themselves, so let them update it. Open the partner, and find the Permissions card.
Turn on "Allow partner to update pipeline status." Their team can then change a lead's phase, close date and close value.
It helps to set up the lead phases you want your resellers to use. They're under Configure, in the Leads menu.
If you use HubSpot or Pipedrive, you map these phases to your CRM's stages.
Then turn on two-way sync. Your resellers' updates reach your CRM, so your team can follow each deal there.
Here's Hannah Calder at Calder and Finch. She opens her lead, and moves it to Free Account.
Her screens show margin, too.
Some reseller programs work the other way. You bill the customer, then pay the reseller their margin. For that, choose You as who collects.
Margin rates live in your partner tiers, under Program Details. They're only paid out when you collect.
Now let's add a payout on a won lead. We'll enter the month's revenue.
The payout reads like a receipt: the revenue, the margin rate, the wholesale price, and the margin you owe the partner.
Not every partner resells. A partner group can use a different model. Inherit follows your portal default, which is now Reseller.
Ledgerwick's Referral Partners only refer customers, so we'll set this group to Referral.
You can also set the model for one partner, on their Margin Details card.
And a single lead can have its own model, too.
That's how to set up reseller partners. Thanks for watching.

metadata.title: AWS re:Invent 2025 - Driving business outcomes with complete AWS Marketplace solutions (PEX111)
metadata.author: AWS Events
metadata.shortDescription:
Organizations are increasingly seeking complete, ready-to-deploy solutions rather than individual products. Learn how AWS Marketplace empowers Partners to deliver comprehensive business solutions that include multiple software products and professional services. This powerful capability enables buyers to procure complete, outcome-focused solutions through a streamlined experience. Whether you're an ISV adding professional services to your software, a systems integrator building solutions, or a buyer looking to simplify procurement, discover how the solution-centric approach in AWS Marketplace helps accelerate digital transformation while reducing procurement complexity.

Learn more:
More AWS events: https://go.aws/3kss9CP 

Subscribe:
More AWS videos: http://bit.ly/2O3zS75
More AWS events videos: http://bit.ly/316g9t4

ABOUT AWS:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) hosts events, both online and in-person, bringing the cloud computing community together to connect, collaborate, and learn from AWS experts.
 AWS is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform, offering over 200 fully featured services from data centers globally. Millions of customers—including the fastest-growing startups, largest enterprises, and leading government agencies—are using AWS to lower costs, become more agile, and innovate faster.

#AWSreInvent #AWSreInvent2025 #AWS

metadata.title: Reselling Professional Services in AWS Marketplace | Amazon Web Services
metadata.author: Amazon Web Services
metadata.shortDescription:
AWS Marketplace sellers, including independent software vendors (ISVs), consulting partners and channel partners, can resell third-party professional services in AWS Marketplace. With this release, AWS Marketplace sellers can authorize other sellers to receive wholesale pricing on professional services, enabling sellers to offer support or implementation services in addition to software in AWS Marketplace. In this video, you’ll get an overview of AWS Marketplace Professional Services and Channel Partner Private Offers (CPPO). You’ll also see a step-by-step walkthrough of how to create a CPPO for professional services and the relevant use cases.

To learn more, visit the AWS Marketplace Seller Guide: https://go.aws/3Qva0RZ

metadata.title: AWS re:Invent 2025 - Solution-based selling strategies in AWS Marketplace (PEX110)
metadata.author: AWS Events
metadata.shortDescription:
Learn about new selling capabilities in AWS Marketplace. This session explores best practices for selling comprehensive solutions, including real-world patterns, contract structures, and technical considerations. Discover how to maximize your AWS Marketplace presence and streamline customer procurement through effective solution-based strategies.

Learn more:
More AWS events: https://go.aws/3kss9CP 

Subscribe:
More AWS videos: http://bit.ly/2O3zS75
More AWS events videos: http://bit.ly/316g9t4

ABOUT AWS:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) hosts events, both online and in-person, bringing the cloud computing community together to connect, collaborate, and learn from AWS experts.
 AWS is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform, offering over 200 fully featured services from data centers globally. Millions of customers—including the fastest-growing startups, largest enterprises, and leading government agencies—are using AWS to lower costs, become more agile, and innovate faster.

#AWSreInvent #AWSreInvent2025 #AWS

This briefing offers a defensive framework for IT leaders and procurement managers managing complex software relationships. We break down common vendor sales tactics that use pressure and misinformation to force unfavorable renewals. By understanding how these teams operate, you can maintain control of your budget and avoid unwanted subscription traps.

We examine how to identify cognitive biases that lead to poor decision-making during negotiations and how to guard against unauthorized procurement bypasses that undermine your authority. You will learn to implement key contract controls that safeguard against vendor overreach. Applying these methods helps your team stay objective when evaluating vendor demands and maintain long-term operational stability.

metadata.title: Meet the Expert: How TD SYNNEX services help partners scale and grow
metadata.author: TD SYNNEX
metadata.shortDescription:
Building your own support and managed services capabilities takes significant investment in people, technology, processes and expertise. But partners don’t have to build everything themselves.
In this Meet the Expert episode, Mark Best explores how TD SYNNEX Services helps partners scale their capabilities, get to market faster and deliver more for their customers.
Discover how TD SYNNEX can help partners:
• Access scalable support and managed services capabilities
• Keep their best people focused on sales, pre-sales and customer engagement
• Expand their services portfolio without building every capability internally
• Reduce the cost and risk associated with service delivery
• Create new revenue and recurring revenue opportunities
• Leverage TD SYNNEX’s European and global service capabilities
• Support customers across networking, cybersecurity, cloud, data centre and more
The business outcomes are clear: grow faster, reduce risk and drive profitability.
Speak to your local TD SYNNEX representative to explore how TD SYNNEX Services can help your business scale.

metadata.shortDescription:
What if you could spend less time managing transactions and more time growing your business?

At TD SYNNEX Inspire 2026, Russell Rabane explores how PartnerFirst is transforming the digital customer experience by bringing together tools, integrations and AI-powered capabilities designed to make doing business easier.

From streamlined quoting and ordering to real-time business insights and cloud management, discover how TD SYNNEX is helping customers work more efficiently across the platforms they already use.

In this session:
- How PartnerFirst Commerce simplifies quoting, ordering, tracking and renewals
- How Digital Bridge connects TD SYNNEX capabilities with everyday business platforms
- The role of AI agents and Model Context Protocol (MCP) in automating workflows
- How StreamOne simplifies cloud purchasing, billing and management
- Why digital adoption can help accelerate business growth

Explore how a more connected digital experience can help you simplify operations, save time and focus on what matters most: your customers.
https://www.tdsynnex.com/na/us/en/partnerfirst.html

#TDSYNNEXInspire #PartnerFirst #DigitalTransformation

metadata.title: Your Next $1M Customer Might Already Be Yours | Inspire 2026 | TD SYNNEX's Inspire Tech Talk
metadata.author: TD SYNNEX
metadata.shortDescription:
What if your next million-dollar customer is already doing business with you?

At TD SYNNEX Inspire 2026, Jessica Ash and Shiloh Roquette explore how IT solution providers can unlock new revenue opportunities within their existing customer relationships by connecting AI, cloud, cybersecurity, infrastructure and services.

Instead of focusing on individual products or vendors, discover how a business outcome-driven approach can help customers solve bigger challenges while creating new opportunities for growth.

=In this session:
- Why your next major growth opportunity may already exist within your customer base
- How to identify cross-selling opportunities across AI, cloud, security and services
- Turning a single technology request into a broader business solution
- How TD SYNNEX High Growth Vendor Solutions helps customers connect technologies around business outcomes
- Why asking the right follow-up questions can uncover additional revenue opportunities

Learn how to move beyond individual transactions, strengthen customer relationships and unlock more value from the customers you already serve.

#TDSYNNEXInspire #CustomerGrowth #AISolutions

metadata.title: Why Cloud Consumption Fraud Is Becoming a Bigger Business Risk
metadata.author: TD SYNNEX
metadata.shortDescription:
What happens when a single compromised credential results in a seven-figure invoice? As cloud adoption grows, so does the opportunity for fraud.

In this episode of The High-Growth Equation, Lawrence Roberts talks with Drew Simonis, Senior Vice President and Chief Information Security Officer at TD SYNNEX, about the growing threat of cloud consumption fraud, why partners are often left carrying the financial burden and how proactive security, customer verification and cloud governance practices can help reduce risk before small issues become costly mistakes.

The conversation explores the tactics attackers are using today, the realities of partner liability and the steps organizations can take to better protect their business and customers.

metadata.title: The Space Economy: New Opportunities for the IT Channel | Tech Talk
metadata.author: TD SYNNEX
metadata.shortDescription:
The space economy is expanding, and new opportunities are emerging for IT solution providers.

At TD SYNNEX Inspire 2026, attendees discovered how the commercialization of space is creating demand for IT infrastructure, connectivity, cybersecurity and services.

This Tech Talk explores the shift from government-led space exploration to commercial innovation, the growing role of technology distribution and how resellers can begin building a space technology strategy.

In this session:
- How the commercial space economy is evolving
- Where IT solution providers can find new opportunities
- Why space technology requires familiar IT capabilities
- How TD SYNNEX is supporting partner education and enablement
- Practical steps to explore the space technology market

Learn how the technologies and expertise you already provide could help support the next frontier of innovation.

https://www.tdsynnex.com/na/us/innovation/space-tech/

#TDSYNNEXInspire #SpaceTechnology #ITChannel

Watch this video to understand what is a FinOps Scope: A segment of technology-related spending to which FinOps Practitioners apply FinOps concepts.

FinOps Scopes frames the way practitioners use FinOps concepts to ingest, analyze, and report on other IT cost and usage spending at their organizations. We've learned from the State of FinOps 2025 and practitioner trends that they're now using FinOps concepts to better understand SaaS, Licensing, AI, data center, and other technology consumption data beyond cloud.

This video references the 2025 definition of FinOps Scopes as delivered at FinOps X Day London 2025.

https://www.finops.org/community/topics/
https://www.finops.org/topic/scopes/

metadata.title: Licensing and SaaS at Scale: Cloud+ FinOps Scopes Intersecting with ITAM & SAM
metadata.author: FinOps Foundation
metadata.shortDescription:
Dieter Matzion of Roku shows how Roku manages 40+ vendors as part of the Cloud Center of Excellence. He goes over negotiation best practices, how legal reviews work, the different signature processes, and how procurement works, including purchase requisitions and how to reference Purchase Order (PO) numbers on invoices.

#ITAM #finopsx #finops

metadata.title: SaaS Contract Management, License Management & Renewal Management (Explained)
metadata.author: Venduris
metadata.shortDescription:
SaaS contract management, SaaS license management and SaaS renewal management explained in five minutes: what to track in every software contract, how to find licenses you pay for but don't use, and how to act before the notice window closes and a contract auto-renews.
 
Most companies don't overspend on software because they negotiate badly. They overspend because renewals arrive before anyone has looked at them. This video walks through the three disciplines that fix that, with a practical routine you can start this week.
 
CHAPTERS
0:00 Why software costs rise at renewal
0:55 SaaS contract management: what to track in every contract
2:05 SaaS license management: finding unused seats
3:15 SaaS renewal management: work back from the notice deadline
4:20 Three steps to start this week
 
WHAT YOU'LL LEARN
• SaaS contract management: the five terms to track in every contract (renewal date, notice period, auto-renewal clause, price escalator, exit rights), and why the latest amendment matters
• SaaS license management: how to compare paid seats with active users and spot inactive, underused and duplicate licenses
• SaaS renewal management: a simple 90/60-day timeline, and why every contract needs one named owner
 
FREE GUIDES
SaaS contract management: https://venduris.com/saas-contract-management
SaaS license management: https://venduris.com/saas-license-management
SaaS renewal management: https://venduris.com/saas-renewal-management
The Venduris Index (how fair are your vendors' renewal terms?): https://venduris.com/fairness-score
 
ABOUT VENDURIS
Venduris is a renewal intelligence platform for SaaS and AI contracts. It helps finance, IT and procurement teams see what renews, when, and whether it is worth renewing, before the notice window closes. https://venduris.com
 
This video is presented by an AI narrator.
 
#SaaSManagement #Procurement #SaaS

segments.text: Most companies don't overspend on software because they negotiate badly.
They overspend because a renewal arrives before anyone has looked at it.
In the next five minutes, we'll cover the three things that fix that:
SaaS contract management, SaaS license management and SaaS renewal management.
Here's a familiar example.
A software contract renews in February.
The notice window closed in December, during the holidays.
The new invoice is fourteen percent higher, for forty seats, while only twenty people actually use the tool.
Gartner has warned that companies without central visibility over
SaaS overspend by at least twenty-five percent, through unused licenses and overlapping tools.
Let's start with the foundation: SaaS contract management.
You can't manage a renewal if you don't know what the contract says.
Every SaaS contract has five terms worth tracking.
First, the renewal date.
Second, the notice period: how many days before renewal you must cancel or renegotiate.
That's often thirty, sixty or ninety days, and it's the real deadline.
Third, the auto-renewal clause, which renews the contract for another full term if nobody acts.
Fourth, the price escalator, which allows an increase at renewal, sometimes on the list price rather than your discount.
And fifth, termination and exit rights.
One more thing: these terms don't always live in one document.
An amendment or a later order form can change the renewal date or the
notice period, so always read the latest signed paper, not the first contract you find.
Next: SaaS license management.
This is where most of the waste hides.
Licenses drift.
People join, change teams and leave, but seats rarely get removed.
Before every renewal, compare the seats you pay for with the people who actually used the tool in the last ninety days.
Look for three things.
Inactive users who haven't logged in at all.
Underused users on a premium tier who only need a basic one.
And duplicates: the same person paying for the same tool in two workspaces.
The gap between paid seats and active seats is your strongest
negotiating point, and it doesn't depend on the vendor agreeing with you.
It's simply what you use.
Which brings us to SaaS renewal management: turning contract terms and usage data into a decision, on time.
Work backwards from the notice deadline, not the renewal date.
Around ninety days before it, pull the contract terms and the usage data.
Around sixty days, decide: renew as is, right-size the seats, renegotiate, or exit.
Then open the conversation with the vendor early, before their team starts the clock on you.
And give every contract one named owner, so the decision never falls between finance, IT and the team using the tool.
If you do nothing else this week, do three things.
List your ten largest software contracts.
For each one, find the notice deadline in the latest signed document.
And name one owner for each.
That alone will catch most renewals before they catch you.
Venduris is a renewal intelligence platform that brings these three steps together for SaaS and AI contracts.
You'll also find free guides and the Venduris Index, which scores how fair vendors' renewal terms are, at venduris.com.

metadata.title: FinOps Forward 2026: FinOps Foundation Keynote
metadata.author: Flexera | ITAM, FinOps & SaaS Management
metadata.shortDescription:
The State of FinOps 2026 reveals how AI, expanded scope, and technology value are reshaping cost management.

Learn how FinOps teams are evolving beyond cloud optimisation to manage AI, SaaS, and enterprise technology spend.

In this session, Steve Trask, COO of the FinOps Foundation, walks through the key findings from the State of FinOps Report 2026, based on insights from practitioners managing over $83 billion in cloud spend worldwide.

You’ll learn:

- How FinOps teams are structured and where they report across organisations
- Why AI cost management is now the most in-demand FinOps skill
- How FinOps scope continues to expand into SaaS, data centres, software, and AI
- The rising importance of allocation, unit economics, and automation
- Why optimisation funds AI initiatives—and why automation is essential for mature teams
- How FinOps is becoming a cultural, organisation‑wide discipline

The session also explores the growing role of AI for FinOps, including tagging, forecasting, optimisation, and automation—along with the challenges of aligning AI cost with business value.
Whether you’re new to FinOps or leading a mature practice, this session provides a clear snapshot of where the discipline is headed and how leading organisations are adapting.

👉 Download the full State of FinOps Report 2026 and explore the interactive data at data.finops.org.

Timestamps:

00:00 – State of FinOps 2026: Why this year matters
01:06 – How FinOps teams are structured and where they report
03:49 – Skills, collaboration, and expanding FinOps scope
09:25 – FinOps for AI, AI for FinOps, and unit economics
10:33 – FinOps scope expansion: SaaS, data centres, and labour spend
17:08 – AI spend becomes standard + the hard problems (value + allocation)
26:05 – Key takeaways: AI dominance and FinOps as a cultural discipline

#itam, #FinOps, #SaaSOptimization, #Flexera, #StateOfFinOps, #FinOpsForAI, #CloudCostManagement, #UnitEconomics, #FinOpsFoundation

metadata.title: SaaS Revenue Recognition Explained: IFRS 15 & ASC 606 Case Study
metadata.author: Accounting and Auditing Hub
metadata.shortDescription:
Software as a Service (SaaS) contracts are one of the fastest-growing business models in the world—and an absolute minefield for accountants! How do you recognize revenue when a contract bundles non-refundable setup fees, custom data migration, software access, and premium support all into a single invoice?

In this video, Suresh Periyasamy (CPA, FCA) breaks down a highly complex, multi-element B2B tech contract using the rigorous 5-Step Model under IFRS 15 and US GAAP ASC 606. We walk through the exact journal entries, the math behind price allocation, and how to present Deferred Revenue on the Balance Sheet.

SaaS revenue recognition is highly complex, but mastering it makes you an incredibly valuable asset to any modern tech company!

🔍 What You Will Learn in This Video:

Identify Performance Obligations: How to determine if Setup Fees, Data Migration, and Premium Support are "distinct" services.

Variable Consideration (SLAs): How to handle Service Level Agreement penalties and "The Constraint."

Standalone Selling Price (SSP): The step-by-step math for re-allocating a bundled contract discount.

Journal Entries: How to record Cash, Contract Liabilities (Deferred Revenue), and recognize revenue Over Time.

Top 3 SaaS Accounting Traps: Why you can NEVER recognize setup fees on Day 1!

⏳ Timestamps:
0:00 - The Complexity of SaaS Revenue Recognition
0:55 - The Scenario: CloudNova Solutions
1:50 - Step 2: Identifying Distinct Performance Obligations
3:15 - Step 3: Transaction Price & The SLA Penalty Trap
4:25 - Step 4: Allocating the Price (SSP Math Explained)
6:00 - Step 5: Recognizing Revenue Over Time
6:45 - Year 1 Journal Entries (Deferred Revenue)
8:10 - Balance Sheet Classification (Current vs. Non-Current)
9:00 - The Top 3 SaaS Accounting Traps to Avoid

👨‍🏫 About Your Instructor:
Suresh Periyasamy is a triple-chartered accounting professional dedicated to bridging the gap between textbook theory and real-world application.

CPA – Licensed by Iowa State Board & AICPA Member (USA)
CPA – Member of CPA Ontario (Canada)
FCA – Fellow, Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka

If you found this breakdown helpful, please drop a like and subscribe! If you are a CPA candidate or a finance professional looking for personalized, one-on-one tutoring to master these standards, I am here to help.

Email: spadvisory.co@gmail.com

metadata.title: How to Create a SaaS Customer Case Study
metadata.author: Tom Bruining
metadata.shortDescription:
Customer case studies are powerful marketing assets, but how do you actually create them? In this video, I break down the entire process—from selecting the right customers to conducting interviews, writing compelling stories, and maximizing their impact across your marketing channels.

00:00 - Intro
01:00 - What sort of case study do you need?
02:44 - Finding the right customers for your case study
04:21 - Setting up the call
05:14 - Preparing your questions and structure
07:01 - Software & tools to use
08:38 - Distribution
10:51 - One last thing

What You’ll Learn:

✔️ Why Case Studies Matter – More than just customer stories, they’re strategic marketing tools.
✔️ How to Choose the Right Customers – Find customers who best showcase your product’s value.
✔️ How to Conduct an Interview – Questions, themes, and structuring your conversation for success.
✔️ Best Tools for Recording & Editing – My recommended tools (including Riverside.fm & CapCut).
✔️ How to Repurpose Case Studies – Embed videos, use quotes in emails, social media, and more.
✔️ How to Overcome Common Objections – Use case studies to address potential customer concerns.

Recommended Tools:

🎥 Recording & Transcription: Riverside.fm – High-quality video/audio recording with separate tracks.
✂️ Editing: CapCut – Quick and simple video editing.
✍️ Content Structuring: ChatGPT – Helps distill themes and insights from transcripts.

Why Case Studies Are Essential

Case studies aren’t just for your website—they can help with:
🔹 Sales Enablement – Overcoming objections & proving ROI.
🔹 Marketing Content – Snippets for LinkedIn, Twitter, TikTok & YouTube.
🔹 Product Education – Showing real-world applications of your SaaS product.

💡 Pro Tip: The best case studies align with customer pain points, common objections, and key decision-making moments in the buyer’s journey.

📢 If you found this video helpful, don’t forget to like, comment, and subscribe for more SaaS marketing insights!

metadata.title: Protecting Your Hosting Margin as the Rules of the Game Change
metadata.author: SAMexpert TV – Microsoft Licensing and Cloud
metadata.shortDescription:
Microsoft raises SPLA prices and changes product rules. Providers pass some of the increase to customers and absorb the rest. Customers also move to their own licences, which removes them from the billable base. Most providers track revenue — but not their actual SPLA margin.

➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖

💸 WHAT IT COSTS YOU

🔻 Price increases you can only partly pass on
🔻 Paying monthly for reported capacity you are not using
🔻 Under-reporting that creates a compliance exposure, found later in an audit
🔻 Customers moving to their own licences and reducing your billable revenue
🔻 No separate SPLA profitability figure, so margin loss is not measured

➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖

🎯 IN THIS EVENT, YOU'LL LEARN

✅ Which recent Microsoft price and product changes hit hosting margins hardest
✅ Why both over-reporting and under-reporting cost money, and why reporting tools miss both
✅ How the Flexible Virtualization Benefit and bring-your-own-licence affect what you can bill, and where they stop applying
✅ How to check your reported position before an audit does

➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖

👥 WHO SHOULD ATTEND

▪️ Hosting and cloud business unit leaders
▪️ MSP and ISV owners running hosted services
▪️ SPLA and licensing managers
▪️ Finance teams responsible for hosting profitability

➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖➖

🖐 Protect your hosting margin and stay audit-ready with expert SPLA support. Learn more: https://samexpert.com/services/for-providers/?utm_source=samexperttv&utm_medium=youtube&utm_campaign=protecting-hosting-margin-as-rules-game-change&utm_content=video_description

metadata.title: The AI Era Is Reshaping SaaS Renewals. Is Your Business Ready?
metadata.author: 10K
metadata.shortDescription:
As AI reshapes enterprise software buying, SaaS renewal conversations have become more strategic than ever. Customers aren't just negotiating price. They're evaluating whether their software continues to deliver value.

In this Agentforce demo, see how the **Renewal Optimization Agent**, built with Salesforce Agentforce, Sales Cloud, and Data 360, transforms a routine renewal request into a consultative customer experience.

Watch as the agent:

* Evaluates contract details, renewal timing, and product usage
* Determines whether a downgrade is truly in the customer's best interest
* Calculates potential overage costs
* Recommends the subscription that best fits the customer's needs
* Automatically updates the contract and completes the renewal workflow

Rather than simply processing requests, Agentforce helps customers make informed, data-driven decisions while enabling SaaS companies to reduce churn, identify expansion opportunities, and deliver a more transparent renewal experience.

Interested in exploring AI use cases like this for your organization?

metadata.title: One Vendor Master Across 30 D365 Legal Entities: The Win Was Trust (Case Study)
metadata.author: AVC-Licensing
metadata.shortDescription:
Nearly 8,000 vendor records were mapped to about 6,800 master vendor accounts and shared across 30 D365 legal entities, after five full rehearsals and a production cutover of about four hours. This case study walks through what we found, who decided, how cross-company duplicate record sharing works, and what changed for accounts payable.

Full case study: free to read at avc-labs.com, no signup (link on our channel page).

What it covers:
• Duplicates disagreed: survivors on hold, tax IDs on the record being retired, different bank accounts
• Not every difference is an error: default ledger accounts stay local where charts of accounts differ
• Who decided: the AP team owned every survivor decision; consultants surfaced conflicts and consequences
• Five rehearsals: cleanup encouraged more cleanup, and the final run started with zero known exceptions
• Duplicate record sharing: each company keeps its record, the shared fields stay identical
• The cutover: about four hours in a weekend window, with old vendor references in Fabric and Power BI fixed in about a day

Honest limits: we didn't measure an ROI or a change in processing time. The outcome is what the AP team reported.

Chapters
0:00 30 legal entities
0:20 In plain words
0:39 Scope
0:56 What we found
1:12 Shared or local
1:27 Who decided
1:49 Five rounds
2:08 Duplicate record sharing
2:31 The cutover
2:52 Honest limits
3:03 Bottom line

Next: Part 2, five test rounds that rewrote the method (on our channel).

one supplier network, and vendor lists

The same supplier could have one address

second, and different payment details in
a third.
Which record do you trust?
The honest answer had become it depends
who you ask.
In D365,
every legal entity keeps its own vendor
records.
A group buying from the same suppliers

Vendor consolidation decides which copy

across 30 legal entities

Five full rehearsals,

disagreed.

accounts.

shared and what stays local.
The AP team owned every business
decision, which records belong together
and which one survives.
Our consultants and developers checked

By the final rehearsal, execution

entities.
Each company keeps its own vendor
record.

A contact change is made once,

What the AP team reported was this.
They could finally trust and navigate

Deduplication counts rows. A vendor
master is a control the business relies
on.

The key thing to remember is this, a vendor relationship doesn't really end when the contract expires. It ends when all access is removed and the risk is fully closed. And if you want to make this process much easier, Safe Security's 100% autonomous platform that can help you manage vendor risk and ensure safe offboarding. metadata.title: 5 Things Every Channel Partner Program Needs
metadata.author: Viktor from Sales
metadata.shortDescription:
Channel Sales AKA Partnerships aren’t this magical revenue stream that you set and forget.

If you’ve sold through Value Added Resellers and System Integrators before you know that most won’t be interested in dealing with you.

Sure, they might sign a contract with you so they have a shiny new thing to show off on their website but never actually make a sale for you.

You get angry and go on to build an army of partners and realise that they’re cannibalising your business by competing on price. That’s the kind of frustration you face if you’re trying to wing it in indirect sales.

But luckily there’s a practice that works and it starts by building a Partner Program.

Today I’m joined by Jani Vrancsik who has 6 years of experience under his belt as a Partnership Manager. Experience which he earned from leading Partnership teams at 3 different tech startups. Let’s welcome him and see how to build a Partnership program that actually works!

#channelsales #techsales #enterprisesales

segments.text: - [Tyler] Hi there,
this is Tyler from the AWS Marketplace team.
In this video, we are going to talk about how to register
as an AWS Marketplace seller.
This includes a brief overview
of our registration requirements
and instructions to get started.
All right, let's jump right in.
There are different registration requirements based
on where you or your company resides
and what type of products you're selling.
Now, to sell paid software licenses in AWS Marketplace,
you must be a permanent resident, a citizen,
or a business entity organized or incorporated
in one of our eligible jurisdictions.
Please take a moment to review our current list
of eligible jurisdictions.
If you are only publishing free software products,
you do not have to be located
in one of our eligible jurisdictions
or provide payment information to AWS Marketplace.
Now, to create and offer free software products
in our digital catalog,
you must sell publicly available,
full-feature, production-ready software,
have a defined customer support process
and support organization,
and provide a means to keep software regularly updated
and free of vulnerabilities.
Now, to be able to register as a seller in AWS Marketplace,
you have to sign in to an AWS account.
You can use an existing AWS account
or create a new account under an organization.
Whichever account you choose,
it will be the seller of record account.
We recommend creating a new AWS account
because all AWS Marketplace interactions will be tied
to this account moving forward.
Sellers have told us that separating production accounts
from the seller of record account simplifies management
and separates disbursements received
from AWS Marketplace sales.
It also provides an additional layer of security
as multiple AWS accounts can be used
to further separate environments
and permissions across teams.
This is not necessary but highly recommended.
Keep in mind, there is no charge or fee
to register as a seller in AWS Marketplace.
Once you've signed into your AWS account,
head over to the AWS Marketplace homepage
via the following URL: aws.amazon.com/marketplace.
Once here, navigate to the Sell in AWS Marketplace tab,
which is located on the top right-hand side of our menu bar.
This page includes helpful resources
for current and prospect sellers,
like educational materials and key seller references.
Go ahead and bookmark this page for future reference.
Next, click Register now.
You will then be directed to the seller registration page
in the AWS Marketplace Management Portal.
This portal is where you will complete your registration,
submit and manage product listings,
monitor the status of your requests,
and measure performance of your AWS Marketplace business.
You must review
and complete the following sections on this page.
Review your legal business name.
This name is shown on communications
between you and buyers
and between you and AWS Marketplace.
Next, review and accept our seller terms and conditions.
These terms and conditions govern your relationship
between buyers and AWS Marketplace.
Please review this documentation thoroughly
and download the PDF version
for local storing and future reference.
Once you've reviewed and accepted the terms and conditions,
the next section is about yourself.
Please answer the following questions
as it relates to your business purpose
for registering as a seller.
Questions include what types of products
you intend on selling,
what pricing models you plan to support,
what category best describes your products or services,
and which industry segment you provide solutions for.
After you've completed these sections,
you will then be able to register
and sign into the AWS Marketplace Management Portal.
If you would like to learn more about our requirements
and steps to get registered as a seller,
please review our Seller Guide.
And, of course, if you have any questions at all
once you have access
to the AWS Marketplace Management Portal,
feel free to contact our Managed Catalog Operations Team
via this link below.
All right, that is all for today.
Thank you for watching and we'll see you next time.

metadata.title: CSP Reseller Partners: New Microsoft Requirements
metadata.author: Manage Protect
metadata.shortDescription:
Microsoft has announced changes to its Cloud Solution Provider program that will impact Indirect Resellers.  There are new requirements to remain a Microsoft CSP Reseller and, potentially, eligibility for any incentives. To remain an authorised reseller, you must:
1. Complete Microsoft's business vetting process 
2.  Be recognised by Microsoft in generating $1,550 in revenue over a 12 month period 
3. Sign the Indirect Reseller Microsoft Partner Agreement
4. Meet the mandatory requirements of the Partner Security Score 
This will impact your ability to acquire and offer Microsoft licencing. 
This video will give you a rundown of the new Microsoft CSP requirements, deadlines and what you need to do.

metadata.title: From Data to Decisions: Smarter Partner Growth with AI | Tech Talk
metadata.author: TD SYNNEX
metadata.shortDescription:
What if your business data could help you identify your next opportunity before your next partner conversation?

At TD SYNNEX Inspire 2026, Jeremiah Barnes and Beau Garrett explore how the Partner Health & Fitness Intelligence Hub is helping customers and vendors turn channel data into more actionable business insights.

Integrated into the event experience, the Intelligence Hub uses data-driven recommendations, benchmarking and machine learning to help partners identify opportunities, strengthen relationships and make more informed decisions.

In this session:
- How Partner Health & Fitness 2.0 goes beyond traditional revenue-based segmentation
- Using machine learning and channel insights to identify growth opportunities
- How personalized recommendations can improve event experiences
- Benchmarking performance and identifying opportunities across vendor relationships
- Turning data into more purposeful business conversations

Discover how better intelligence can help partners move from instinct to informed action.

https://www.tdsynnex.com/na/us/en/partnerfirst.html

#TDSYNNEXInspire #DataAnalytics #PartnerGrowth

metadata.author: CFO AI
metadata.shortDescription: These sources provide a comprehensive technical guide to NetSuite’s Advanced Revenue Management (ARM) module, detailing the lifecycle of revenue from initial setup to final recognition. The documentation explains how to configure item revenue categories, define fair value formulas, and establish revenue recognition rules that trigger either actual or forecast plans. Key processes such as merging revenue arrangements, managing advanced cost amortization, and performing bulk edits are explored to ensure financial compliance and accuracy. Additionally, the materials outline the necessity of accounting periods and specific permissions required to view, edit, or delete revenue records. By covering both automated updates and manual overrides, the sources illustrate how to maintain a precise audit trail for complex sales contracts and subscriptions.

metadata.title: Consumption Based Revenue Recognition: ASC 606 & Usage-Based Pricing (SaaS & Cloud Accounting)
metadata.author: Ambition, Aligned with Devon Coombs
metadata.shortDescription:
Are you struggling to account for usage-based pricing under ASC 606? The shift from flat-rate SaaS subscriptions to consumption-based revenue models is the single biggest disruption in tech accounting today.

In this deep dive, we explore why "Stand Ready" obligations (ratable recognition) vs. "Specified Service" obligations (consumption recognition) create massive diversity in practice—and why Big Tech companies like AWS, Google, and Microsoft likely report revenue completely differently.

IN THIS EPISODE: 0:00 - The "Ivory Tower" of Accounting Policies 2:15 - SaaS vs. Consumption: The Shift in Business Models 6:45 - Technical Accounting: Stand Ready vs. Specified Service 11:30 - Variable Consideration: The Nightmare of Overages 16:20 - The "Daisy Chain" Effect: Cumulative Catch-up Risks 21:10 - RPO & Breakage: Estimating Unused Credits 26:00 - System Failures: Why ERPs Can't Handle Consumption Data

KEY TOPICS COVERED:

Revenue Recognition: How to choose between ratable recognition (with estimated overages) vs. pure consumption models.

ASC 606 Variable Consideration: The risks of estimating overages and the downstream impact on cumulative catch-ups.

Contract Modifications: How to handle price changes and tier adjustments without restating historical revenue.

Financial Reporting: Why comparability between major cloud providers (AWS, Azure, GCP) is nearly impossible.

ABOUT THE HOSTS:

Angela Liu: Founder of the Gap Savvy Community, ex-KPMG (Audit/Advisory/National Office), and former finance leader at Glassdoor and Everest Systems.

Devon Coons: Ex-Controller at Google Cloud, Financial Advisor to the Office of the CFO, and Lecturer at San Jose State University.

👇 JOIN THE DEBATE Is your finance team recognizing usage-based revenue ratably or based on actual consumption? Let us know in the comments!

#SaaSAccounting #ASC606 #RevenueRecognition #UsageBasedPricing #ConsumptionModel #FinOps #CFO #TechnicalAccounting #GapSavvy #DevonCoons

metadata.title: The modern way to work with vendors in NetSuite: Faster onboarding, smoother invoices
metadata.author: Charted (formerly SquareWorks)
metadata.shortDescription:
Vendor information is one of the hidden pain points of AP, with friction a common occurrence across purchasing, invoice processing, and payments. For many NetSuite teams, manual vendor onboarding leads to incomplete records, missing details, and downstream invoice delays that slow everything else.

In this session, we’ll explore a modern approach to working with vendors in NetSuite, starting with faster, simpler onboarding that sets AP up for smoother invoice processing from day one. By capturing accurate vendor, tax, and payment details upfront, finance teams reduce rework, shorten invoice cycle times, and maintain strong controls as they scale globally.

➤ SHOW NOTES / FULL RECAP:
The takeaway guide Chris mentions: "Stop chasing vendors for payment details: A NetSuite-native guide for friction-free vendor onboarding" → https://charted.com/resources/?_categories=white-papers-ebooks&utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=video

CHAPTERS
0:00 What will this vendor onboarding session cover — and who's presenting?
3:55 Why is vendor onboarding the most overlooked part of AP?
5:46 Spreadsheet or vendor portal — why do both break down at scale?
7:12 How does one wrong bank detail ripple through payments, matching, and close?
8:53 How do I build the business case for fixing vendor onboarding?
10:56 What should a modern vendor onboarding experience actually look like?
12:25 What does Advanced Vendor Onboarding look like inside NetSuite?
15:57 How do I map form fields to my NetSuite vendor record — including custom fields?
16:40 How do I create a vendor and send them an onboarding form?
18:48 What does the vendor see, and can anyone else open that link?
20:01 How do I review and approve changes before they hit the vendor record?
21:12 Once onboarding is complete, how fast can I actually pay them?
22:32 Where does vendor onboarding fit in the rest of the AP workflow?
24:32 Can I use this to update information for existing vendors?
27:48 What vendor onboarding metrics can I report on in NetSuite?

We have, like, we have a regular standard template but in order to if you wanna add, subtract differentiate just change your fields, your look and feel of it, add new fields, add new dropdowns, you can do so fairly easily through the advanced onboarding service. If you want something a little bit more customized and we also have, like, an implementation team can really help you kind of finely tune things as well for a new template. But when you are creating a new field, so you can just say, like, custom field you basically just label it Label is here, and then you can see there's different types. metadata.title: Supplier Onboarding with Zero Retyping | NetSuite + Docusign
metadata.author: Agreement Automation Lab
metadata.shortDescription:
To onboard a supplier, you chase a signed agreement and then type their legal name and tax ID into NetSuite. In this video your supplier types those details once, in the agreement, and the workflow copies them to the vendor record. The video runs a Docusign Workflow Builder workflow on a NetSuite sandbox.

The workflow:
- reads the vendor and its contact from NetSuite
- fills the supplier onboarding agreement and emails it to your supplier
- collects the legal name, tax ID, entity type and founding year, then the signature
- waits for your procurement team to countersign
- writes the legal name and tax ID to the vendor record and files the signed agreement

Set up the NetSuite app for Docusign IAM: https://fluidlabs.com/documentation/netsuite-for-docusign-iam
See how NetSuite connects to Docusign: https://fluidlabs.com/integrations/platforms/netsuite
Import more workflows: https://fluidlabs.com/workflows

Chapters
0:00 Supplier onboarding, the manual way
0:21 The workflow in Docusign Workflow Builder
0:38 Starting the workflow
0:58 The supplier adds legal and tax details and signs
1:39 Procurement countersigns
2:00 Back in NetSuite: the vendor record, updated
2:12 The signed agreement, filed

In daily use, you start this workflow from the vendor record in NetSuite with the Baton Launcher, the Fluidlabs browser extension. The video starts it from Docusign.

Fluidlabs, a Docusign Build IAM Specialized Partner, built and recorded this video. An AI voice reads the narration. Honeycomb Mfg. and its suppliers are made up, and so is every record you see. Ask your lawyer to review any document before you use it. Docusign used to call Workflow Builder "Maestro". Docusign is a trademark of Docusign, Inc. Oracle and NetSuite are registered trademarks of Oracle and/or its affiliates.
